summary.title: An Investigation of the KF-type Lorentz-Symmetry Breaking Gauge Models in N = 1-Supersymmetric Scenario
summary.authors: H. Belich, G. S. Dias, J.A. Helayel-Neto, F.J.L. Leal, W. Spalenza
summary.field_subfield: Theoretical Physics: Supersymmetry and Lorentz Violation
summary.executive_summary: This paper investigates the incorporation of Kostelecký's (KF-type) Lorentz-symmetry breaking (LSB) into an N=1 supersymmetric framework. The authors propose two distinct mechanisms to generate the background tensor Kµνκλ required for LSB: one utilizing a chiral superfield and the other a vector superfield. In the chiral scenario, the background vector is derived from the gradient of a complex scalar field, resulting in a specific form for Kµνκλ dependent solely on the scalar component. In the vector scenario, a real vector superfield accommodates the background vector, yielding the standard K-tensor form with richer fermionic content. This paper investigates the incorporation of Kostelecký's (KF-type) Lorentz-symmetry breaking (LSB) into an N=1 supersymmetric framework. The authors propose two distinct mechanisms to generate the background tensor Kµνκλ required for LSB: one utilizing a chiral superfield and the other a vector superfield. In the vector scenario, a real vector superfield accommodates the background vector, yielding the standard K-tensor form with richer fermionic content. The study demonstrates that while the models preserve the superspace formulation, the non-zero vacuum expectation values of the background fields spontaneously break both Lorentz symmetry and supersymmetry. The authors analyze the resulting component actions, identifying mixing terms between gauge fields and their superpartners that could lead to mass splittings.
